name: Viana do Castelo – Cabedelo
notes: Windiest spot in the north (summer nortada, often 25 kn): kite at the north end of Cabedelo behind the big breakwater (flat water) or ride the waves outside. Schools on the beach; some rocks in the water; busy in summer. Also: Caminha – Moledo (waves).

name: Esposende – Ofir
notes: Flat knee-deep lagoon in the Cávado estuary behind the Ofir sandspit: reached by boat only (school transfer from Esposende port), nature reserve; strong current and boat traffic at the river mouth. Waves on the sea side, over the dunes. Pin is the sea beach: the lagoon has no OSM element.

name: Murtosa – Ria de Aveiro
notes: Flat standing-depth lagoon at Praia do Bico (Murtosa), Clube Nortada school on site. Southerlies in winter blow onshore; summer thermal wind is strong, so small kites. Slippery mussel bed (wear shoes); power cable just downwind of the road launch in westerlies. Ankle deep at low tide.

name: Lagoa de Óbidos
notes: Flat, waist-deep lagoon; lighter wind (big kites). Guides report kiting closed in summer (about 15 Jun–15 Sep) near the mouth and in the north of the lagoon: then ride by the sailing school or at Bom Sucesso. Also: Peniche – Baleal (ocean). Summer ban reported by a guide only: no official text found.

name: Guincho
notes: Very strong nortada (25–35 kt in summer), waves, rocks in the middle of the bay: advanced riders. Schools on the beach (Gustykite, Nortada Aventura). Inside the Sintra-Cascais natural park: one guide says a permit or club membership may be needed, ask a school. Kite to the north side to keep clear of the surf line-up.

name: Fonte da Telha
notes: Closest spot to Lisbon; all levels, lighter wind, small to medium waves; schools on the beach (Wind Spirit Club, Gustykite). Very busy in summer: ride a bit north or south of the crowd. Nova Vaga, 8 km north, is the official kite beach of Costa da Caparica.

name: Alcochete
notes: Flat, shallow water on the Tagus estuary across from Lisbon (Praia dos Moinhos); beginner friendly, school on site. Stones; mud flats at low tide; water quality varies. Alkitesurf school at Praia dos Moinhos (Time Out Lisboa).

name: Lagoa de Albufeira
notes: Flat-water lagoon behind the sandbar; school on site (Meira Pro Center); too shallow at low tide and in dry summers, deeper on the east side. Watch for swimmers in summer.

name: Lagos – Meia Praia
notes: Long sandy bay east of Lagos with kite schools on the beach. Works in thermal S, SE and E winds (waves build with swell from SW to SE). The usual summer N wind (Nortada) blows offshore: beginners only with school cover, otherwise very experienced riders.

name: Alvor
notes: Ria de Alvor: flat, mostly waist-deep lagoon; schools run a boat from Alvor to a sandbar in the lagoon, others walk a boardwalk from the beach car park. NW thermal, gusty near the edges; water from mid tide. Submerged hazards and currents in the channels.

name: Porto Santo
